lines.text: There is a book, around 600 years old, that nobody on Earth can read.
Every page is written in a script that no one has ever identified.
Carbon dating puts its pages between 1404 and 1438.
It's packed with plants nobody can identify, strange star charts, and tiny figures bathing in pools.
Codebreakers from both World Wars tried to crack it. Every one of them failed.
A book dealer named Wilfrid Voynich bought it in 1912, and it still carries his name.
Today it sits in Yale's rare book library, catalogued as MS 408.
Is it a lost language, a code, or one of history's greatest hoaxes?
Six centuries later, the book is still keeping its secret.

sources.claim: Vellum radiocarbon dated 1404 to 1438 (University of Arizona, 2009); never demonstrably deciphered
WWI and WWII codebreakers including William Friedman studied it unsuccessfully; hoax theories exist
Wilfrid Voynich acquired it in 1912; donated to Yale in 1969; held at Beinecke Library as MS 408

publish.title: The 600-Year-Old Book Nobody Can Read 📜
publish.description: Unknown script, impossible plants, star charts, and codebreakers who all failed. The Voynich manuscript is still unsolved.
